title: Dear Passengers Multiplayer: How Co-op Works + a Free Multiplayer Plane Game
summary: How Dear Passengers co-op works - pilot and cabin crew roles, physics chaos - plus a free multiplayer plane crash game you can play in your browser today.
body_text: Nobody is wishlisting Dear Passengers to play it alone. The entire pitch is co-op: you and your friends are the crew of the world's worst airline, and the game is what happens when everything goes wrong at once. Here's everything known about how Dear Passengers multiplayer works - and a free multiplayer plane crash game you can play in your browser right now. How Dear Passengers co-op works Dear Passengers, from developer FLEXUS, splits the crew across roles: One player takes the cockpit and actually flies the plane through weather, turbulence, and air pockets. Everyone else works the cabin: serving meals, calming passengers, securing cargo, and fixing whatever breaks next. Before takeoff, the crew picks which passengers and cargo to accept - riskier choices pay more, and some crates contain things like live crocodiles. Everything is physics-driven, and the plane pitches under your feet, so even walking down the aisle is a challenge mid-crisis. It's the Overcooked formula strapped to a failing aircraft: divided attention, constant small emergencies, and success depending entirely on how well your group communicates while screaming. The catch: you can't play it yet Dear Passengers is targeting a 2026 release on Steam. There's no demo and no early access - just a wishlist button. Player count hasn't been officially confirmed either. Play a free multiplayer plane crash game right now ATTENTION PASSENGERS is a free browser game inspired by Dear Passengers, and it has a multiplayer mode with a twist: instead of cooperating, you're competing. Everyone is on the same doomed plane, disasters keep hitting, and the goal is to survive longer than the other players - with sabotage very much allowed. Shove debris toward rivals, grab passengers, and be the last one standing when the wreck settles. Play ATTENTION PASSENGERS multiplayer free - browser-based, no download, with a single-player survival mode too if your friends are offline. Fair warning from the developer: multiplayer physics is the hardest thing in this genre to get right, and the multiplayer mode is rougher around the edges than single-player. That's part of the charm - half the fun is the jank. Frequently asked questions Is Dear Passengers online co-op? Yes, it's built around online co-op multiplayer, with one player flying and the others managing the cabin. How many players does Dear Passengers support? An exact count hasn't been confirmed. The structure - one pilot plus a cabin crew - suggests small groups, similar to other co-op chaos games. Does Dear Passengers have a release date? It's targeting 2026 on Steam. See our full explainer for everything known so far. Is there a free multiplayer alternative? Yes - ATTENTION PASSENGERS has a free multiplayer mode where you survive a plane crash and sabotage other players, playable in the browser. How will you renovate your swimming pool?
summary: When it comes to renovating your pool, there are many possibilities. Follow our advice on how to go about it!
body_text: Renovating your swimming pool becomes more and more essential over time. But apart from the liner, which you have to renew regardless after a certain number of years, the possibilities are many. Not sure where to start? Here are our recommendations for the best actions you can take when it's time to renovate your pool and replace its equipment! Renovate to benefit from a more economical pool with better quality water Installing a variable speed pump is one of the best improvements that a pool can enjoy. A pump of this kind rotates water 24h/24 at a low speed: it therefore consumes little energy (up to 70% less than a single speed pump !), enables continuous water filtration and does all this very quietly. Replacing your sand filter with an element filter (with cartridges) is another way of saving money and improving the water filtration quality . A 4-cartridge filter filters the water very finely, which therefore requires less maintenance (treatment products), and can only be rinsed once at the end of the season: much less water (and time) wasted than with the frequent backwashing that comes with a sand filter! Renovate to make pool maintenance easier Imagine no longer needing to check the water quality of your pool, no longer having to control the pump speed yourself, or not even having to monitor the water level in the pool! All of this is possible, e.g. with an automatic water treatment system, which doesn't just inject salt or chlorine at set times, but analyses your water first so that it can then be treated with the right quantity of treatment products. And even more is possible with the installation of an automation system which helps your equipment communicate with itself: an incredibly efficient way of taking a large amount of pool maintenance work off your hands. PH level, quantity of chlorine or salt in the water, pump function, water level...automatically controlled, and can be monitored from your smartphone. Convenient, isn't it? Moreover, a system like this also helps you save money by using the right dose of treatment products at the right time, and only making your equipment function when it's really necessary. Renovate to swim in the pool for longer, in more comfort Making swimming season last longer, and enjoying water at a pleasant and gentle temperature all year round, is possible thanks to the heat pump . This installation is the most virtuous heating system , which creates more heat compared to the energy it uses. An economical way of swimming for as long as possible! But if you really want to do things as efficiently and virtuously as possible, install a cover on your pool first. Because open air water cools down, continuously evaporates and is exposed to UV rays from the sun which destroy the chlorine. A cover should therefore be considered first to have a more comfortable, economical and virtuous pool. Renovate your pool progressively, year by year You don't have to make all these changes at once. It's certainly useful to take advantage of renovating the pool when you need to replace the equipment, but you can also do it on a year-by-year basis to even out costs. It's your pool, so don't hesitate: the latest equipment will be much more convenient for you than older installations, consequently saving you money and making your swimming pool more virtuous than ever before.

title: Which Training Topics Need Animation vs Slide-Style Video?
summary: Choose the right training video format with a practical framework for animation, slide-style video, screenshots, demonstrations, and mixed formats.
body_text: The MOTION decision framework Score no points and invent no false precision. Instead, discuss these six questions with the subject expert and instructional designer. M, Movement Is actual movement, transformation, or timing part of what must be learned? If yes, favour animation, demonstration, or screen recording. If no, a stable visual may be sufficient. O, Observability Can the important event be filmed or captured accurately? Invisible or impossible mechanisms may need explanatory animation. Visible physical skills usually benefit from authentic demonstration. Interface detail usually benefits from real screens. T, Task fidelity How closely must training resemble the performance environment? High-fidelity needs push toward real equipment, interfaces, language, and constraints. Low-fidelity conceptual orientation can use simplified diagrams or animation. Never let style remove cues needed for transfer. I, Inspection Must learners compare, read, calculate, or examine a stable configuration? Use slide-style layouts, static diagrams, downloadable references, or learner-controlled frames. Fast motion makes inspection harder. O, Outcome and risk What happens if the learner misunderstands? Higher-risk topics demand stronger source control, expert review, accessibility checks, and often practice or assessment beyond video. Risk does not automatically determine visual style; it determines evidence and assurance. N, Navigation and maintenance Will learners need to find one fact later? Will the content change frequently? Choose modular scenes, transcripts, chapters, and companion text. A highly animated five-minute sequence may be expensive to update when one number changes. Stable components can be easier to replace, but actual maintainability depends on the tool and source files. Applied examples Fire-extinguisher selection Use slide-style comparison for extinguisher categories and decision criteria. Use demonstration for handling and safe stance. Animation can show consequences or simplified fire behaviour only when technically validated. A video alone should not substitute for required practical training. How a refrigeration cycle works Use animation for refrigerant movement and state changes, with a stable labelled system diagram as an anchor. Pause at meaningful phases. Let narration and highlighting correspond to the same component. Data-protection policy update Use a restrained slide-style structure: what changed, who is affected, required action, and escalation. Add a scenario for a borderline request. Link to the current policy and job aid. CRM opportunity entry Use authentic screen capture or simulation for exact fields and feedback. A slide-style introduction can explain the business rule. Re-record volatile interface scenes without regenerating the durable conceptual section. Difficult customer conversation Use a filmed or animated scenario to show choices, tone, and consequences. Follow it with stable decision prompts and reflection. If realism of facial expression is essential, test whether the chosen animation style carries enough nuance. Organisational induction Slide-style video can orient learners to structure, values, and resources. A presenter may add welcome and credibility. Avoid animated movement that contributes nothing to understanding. Mixed-format storyboarding Do not force an entire course into one visual mode. A storyboard might use a stable diagram for the whole model, animation for one changing process, a real screenshot to connect it to work, and a slide-style recap to stabilise the decision rule. Consistency comes from shared terminology, visual grammar, voice, brand, navigation, and accessibility, not from making every scene move the same way. Multimedia-learning research offers two cautions. First, words and pictures should be designed around how learners process information, not around the prestige of the delivery technology. Second, animation is not automatically superior to static graphics. Learner control, segmentation, signalling, prior knowledge, and the accuracy of the representation affect the result. Accessibility is part of format choice The visual format changes what must be made available in other modes. W3C’s WCAG 2.2 guidance says prerecorded audio in synchronised media requires captions at Level A, except for the stated media-alternative case. Captions include relevant non-speech audio and speaker identification, not only dialogue. At Level AA, important visual information not conveyed in the main soundtrack requires audio description. Plan this in the script: speak essential labels and state changes; do not communicate status by colour alone; give learners enough time to read; provide accurate captions and a useful transcript; avoid flashing and unnecessary motion; use player controls that support pause, replay, and navigation. Narrating the essential action can make a video more robust for many learners, but it does not automatically prove WCAG conformance. Test the finished media and player. For current product options, compare AI video tools for training and education and the best AI training video generators . FAQ Is animation more engaging than slides? Not inherently. Relevant motion can focus attention; decorative motion can distract. Evaluate comprehension and task performance, not assumed engagement. Are slide-style videos just narrated PowerPoints? They can be, but effective slide-style video is designed for asynchronous viewing with concise scenes, purposeful visuals, signalling, and suitable pacing. Can one training video mix animation and slides? Yes. A stable overview followed by an animated process and a slide-style recap is often coherent when each format has a defined job. What format is best for software training? Use authentic screen recording or simulation when interface detail matters, supported by stable diagrams or slides for durable concepts. Plan for software updates. What format is best for compliance training? There is no single best format. Use stable policy summaries, realistic decisions or scenarios, searchable source material, and assessment appropriate to the risk. Choose the evidence learners need The best training video format is the one that reveals the information needed for correct performance with the least unnecessary cognitive and maintenance burden. Animate meaningful change, stabilise material that needs inspection, and use authentic footage when fidelity matters. To prototype both explanatory and presentation-led approaches from existing material, start with Knowlify’s training video maker . Verify current style, input, export, accessibility, and plan capabilities before selecting a format for a full programme. title: The Complete Guide to Payments in Sierra Leone 2026: Virtual Cards, Mobile Money & Visa Fees
summary: Visiting Sierra Leone in 2026? Get visa-on-arrival fees, eVisa timelines, mobile money info, and the best virtual card for paying online abroad.
body_text: Most visitors to Sierra Leone need either a visa on arrival (around USD 80, issued at Lungi International Airport and land borders) or an pre-applied eVisa applied for in advance at (USD 80, roughly 3 business days to process). ECOWAS/African Union citizens often pay less or nothing. Cash still dominates day-to-day spending, but mobile money (Orange Money, Afrimoney) and internationally enabled virtual card providers like Miden are the easiest ways to pay online before and during your trip, from booking hotels to covering conference and MICE event fees. This guide covers everything you need to plan a 2026 trip to Sierra Leone: entry requirements, when to go, what to see, how to pay for things ( choosing the best virtual card provider for international payments ), business and event travel, safety, and answers to the questions people ask most. Banana Island - Sierra Leone 1. Why Visit Sierra Leone in 2026 Sierra Leone is one of West Africa's most underrated destinations. Palm-lined Atlantic beaches, the Freetown Peninsula's forested hills, chimpanzee sanctuaries, and a warm, fast-recovering tourism scene are just a few of the things that make this area memorable. Freetown is also becoming a regional hub for conferences, trade fairs, and NGO/government events, which means more travelers are arriving each year not just for the beaches, but for business. Whether you're coming for River Number 2 Beach, the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, or a multi-day MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) event in Freetown, the big three; visas, money, and payments, are what every traveler needs to sort out first. This guide walks through each one. You Might Also Like: Top 10 places to visit in Sierra Leone 2. Entry Requirements: Visa on Arrival & eVisa in Sierra Leone Sierra Leone offers two main entry routes for tourists and business travelers; a visa on arrival at official ports of entry, and an eVisa applied for online before you fly. Whichever one applies to you depends on your nationality. On-Arrival Visa Sierra Leone: What to Know Available at Freetown International Airport (Lungi) and at land borders including Jendema (Liberia) and Gbalamuya (Guinea). Standard fee is roughly USD 80 for most eligible nationalities (some third-party facilitators quote higher all-in prices, so always check the official rate first). ECOWAS/African Union citizens often pay less — some nationalities are charged around USD 25, and a handful (e.g., Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius) are issued a free visa on arrival under reciprocal agreements. Visas on arrival are typically valid for 30 days, single entry. You'll need: a passport valid 6+ months beyond your stay, proof of onward/return travel, accommodation details, and your yellow fever vaccination card (mandatory, checked on landing). eVisa Option Citizens of countries not eligible for visa-on-arrival must apply for an eVisa in advance through the official portal. Cost is around USD 80, with processing usually completed within a few business days. Apply only through the official government portal — third-party sites often charge extra "service fees" for the same visa. Check your Country’s Visa eligibility here: Sierra Leone Free Visa Eligible Countries Official Embassy Visa Fee Schedule (Washington, D.C.) If you're applying for a Sierra Leone visa in advance through an embassy or consulate rather than on arrival, the Embassy of Sierra Leone in Washington, D.C. publishes the following official fee schedule for visas processed there (fees payable by money order or cashier's check only — non-refundable): Visa Category Single Entry Multiple Entry Requirement Tourist / Visitor $100 $150 Up to 30 days per visit Business $100 $150 Letter from employer required Transit $30 N/A Max 72 hours, onward ticket required Student $75 $100 Enrollment letter required Journalist / Media $100 $150 Press credentials required Diplomatic / Official Gratis Gratis Diplomatic note required Expedited Service (add-on) +$50 +$50 2–3 business days Source: Embassy of Sierra Leone, Washington, D.C. Practical Tip: The embassy's pre-arrival fees ($100–$150) are noticeably higher than the ~$80 figure commonly quoted for the on-arrival visa at Lungi Airport. If your nationality is eligible for visa-on-arrival, applying at Lungi may be cheaper than going through an embassy; if it isn't, you'll need to go through an embassy or the eVisa portal instead. Always confirm the exact, current fee with your nearest Sierra Leone embassy/consulate or directly inside the evisa.sl application before booking your trip. Peninsula Beaches- Sierra Leone 3. Money, Payments & the Best Virtual Cards for Sierra Leone Sierra Leone remains a largely cash-based economy outside major hotels and businesses in Freetown. For anything you need to pay online before or during your trip — flights, hotels, visa fees, conference tickets — a virtual visa card for international payments is generally the fastest, safest option, especially if your home bank card gets blocked for "unusual" overseas or online activity. Local Currency & Cash The Official currency is the Sierra Leonean Leone (SLL). Carry cash (USD or EUR travel in clean, newer bills) for markets, local transport, and smaller restaurants. ATMs exist in Freetown but are not universally reliable outside the capital. Don't depend on them as your only source of funds. Mobile Money Mobile money is the backbone of everyday digital payments in Sierra Leone: Orange Money and Africell's Afrimoney are the two dominant providers, used for everything from utility bills to hotel and restaurant payments. Both now offer prepaid Visa cards linked to mobile money wallets, letting users without a traditional bank account make local and international online payments. A useful context if you're paying local vendors, staff, or partners while in-country. Setting up a local mobile money account as a short-term tourist is possible but usually requires a local SIM and ID, so it's more practical for longer stays, NGO staff, or business travelers than a one-week beach holiday. How to Choose the Best Virtual Card for Online Payments in Sierra Leone Because card acceptance is still uneven and international transfers to Sierra Leone can be slow or costly, many travelers, event organizers, and businesses use a virtual card to handle end-to-end travel logistics. When comparing the best virtual card for online payments in this context, look for: Global acceptance with Visa or Mastercard networks (important since local card infrastructure is still developing) Instant issuance so you're not waiting days before a trip or event deadline. Multi-currency support to avoid repeated conversion fees between USD, EUR, and SLE. Low or no cross-border fees, since you'll likely be paying vendors, hotels, or organizers based outside your home country. Spending controls — the ability to load a fixed amount, which is useful for managing event budgets or per-trip spending caps. Business Travel & MICE Events in Sierra Leone Freetown has increasingly hosted MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) activity: government summits, NGO forums, trade expos, and regional business gatherings. If you're traveling for one of these events in 2026, payments are usually the biggest friction point: Registration and delegate fees are often invoiced in USD but need to be paid from abroad, where local bank transfers can be slow or blocked by compliance checks. Some African Union/ECOWAS citizens pay a reduced fee (around USD 25), and a small number of countries with reciprocal agreements get a free visa on arrival. Fees can change, so confirm the current amount on the official eVisa portal or with your nearest Sierra Leone embassy before you travel. Does Sierra Leone use mobile money? Yes. Mobile money is the primary way most Sierra Leoneans pay for everyday things. Orange Money and Africell's Afrimoney are the two major providers, used for bills, market purchases, transport, and increasingly hotel and restaurant payments.
